# BRAMPP

> BRAMPP is a free, open-source XAMPP/MAMP alternative for macOS. It manages local development
> services (Apache, Nginx, MariaDB/MySQL, PostgreSQL, Redis, PHP-FPM, Node.js, Python, ASP.NET Core)
> through Homebrew — with local domains, automatic HTTPS via mkcert, database tools and a native
> SwiftUI interface. MIT licensed.

Key facts:
- Platform: macOS 14+ (Sonoma), Apple Silicon (arm64) only — native SwiftUI app; Intel Macs are not supported
- Not a binary bundle: it controls the user's existing Homebrew services (`brew services run`)
- Local domains: creates vhosts, /etc/hosts entries and per-domain SSL certificates (mkcert)
- Supported stacks: PHP 8.1–8.5, Node.js, Python (FastAPI/Django/Flask), ASP.NET Core, static/SPA
- Databases: MariaDB/MySQL, PostgreSQL (multi-version), Redis; phpMyAdmin/pgAdmin/Adminer installers
- Languages: English and Turkish UI (runtime switchable)
- MCP server: built-in Model Context Protocol endpoint (http://127.0.0.1:8765/mcp, loopback only,
  off by default) with 22 tools — AI assistants (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, ChatGPT Codex) can
  create/update domains, start and stop app servers, control services, read BRAMPP and per-domain
  logs, list/create databases, run read-only SQL, and dump or restore databases via mysqldump and
  pg_dump; per-scope permissions (Domains, Services, Databases, Logs, Sharing) grant no access / read /
  read+write, and disallowed tools never appear to the client; a fifth scope, Sharing (list_shares/start_share/stop_share), opens a Cloudflare Quick Tunnel to give a local site a temporary public trycloudflare.com address and defaults to NO ACCESS; the native UI reflects every change
  instantly. Two skill files ship with the app — mcptools (general) and brampp_mysql (databases)
- Distribution: signed with a Developer ID Application certificate and notarized by Apple; the
  notarization ticket is stapled to both the app and the DMG, so it verifies even offline — no
  Gatekeeper workaround is needed
- Updates: the app can check GitHub Releases for a newer version on request; it never self-updates,
  the download stays in the user's browser
- License: MIT — Copyright Karaca Teknoloji (Macit Karaca)
- Author: Macit Karaca (https://github.com/macitkaraca), Karaca Technology (https://karacatechnology.com)

- [Install](https://macitkaraca.github.io/brampp/install/): requirements, the four setup steps, signature verification, building from source, troubleshooting
- [MCP server](https://macitkaraca.github.io/brampp/mcp/): all 22 tools by area, the permission model, and how to connect a client
- [Comparison](https://macitkaraca.github.io/brampp/compare/): bundled stacks, PHP-only tools and containers — including when each of those is the better choice
- [Guides hub](https://macitkaraca.github.io/brampp/guides/): practical guides on local development ([Türkçe](https://macitkaraca.github.io/brampp/tr/guides/))
- [Local HTTPS on macOS](https://macitkaraca.github.io/brampp/guides/local-https/): mkcert, the system trust store, .test vs .local
- [Apache and Nginx side by side](https://macitkaraca.github.io/brampp/guides/apache-nginx-together/): port splitting, per-domain routing, reverse proxies
- [MCP for local development](https://macitkaraca.github.io/brampp/guides/mcp-local-dev/): scoped permissions and a safe SQL surface
- [Repository](https://github.com/macitkaraca/brampp): source code, issues, releases

## Comparisons

- vs XAMPP / MAMP: BRAMPP does not bundle Apache, PHP or MySQL binaries — it manages the Homebrew
  formulas already installed on the machine, so there is no second copy to keep in sync.
- vs Laravel Herd / Valet: BRAMPP is framework-agnostic and covers Nginx, PostgreSQL, Redis,
  Node.js, Python and ASP.NET Core alongside PHP; everything is free and MIT licensed.
- vs Docker-based local stacks: no containers, no daemon overhead — native services on the host,
  started per session with `brew services run`.
